mainTopic: Why the חביתין (the כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering) may be prepared on שבת, and how much oil it needs
overview: This amud asks why the חביתין, the כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering, may be prepared on שבת. One answer is that they are like the מנחה of the תמידין. רבא gives another reason: they need a holy vessel, so baking them a day early would make them פסול through לינה. A ברייתא then asks how much oil the חביתין need. It tries comparing them to the מנחת נסכים (three לוגין) and to the מנחת נדבה (one לוג), and each comparison is equally strong. רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה settles it from the word תמיד: three לוגין per עשרון. רבי שמעון reaches the same amount by comparing the חביתין to the sheep's מנחה, since both use one עשרון of flour. The גמרא then asks why the ברייתא seems to contradict itself. אביי, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע and רבה each explain who is speaking in it, and רבה's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The griddle-cakes are like the daily offerings' meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The first explanation ends: the חביתין are treated like the מנחה that comes with the תמידין, so they override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the meal offering of the daily offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that started earlier. It says the חביתין belong in the same group as the תמידין, which are brought even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was how the baking of the חביתין can push aside שבת. This answer compares them to the מנחה of the תמידין. Since the תמידין override שבת, so do the חביתין.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering that comes along with the daily קרבנות
The כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering
It is just like… (it shares the same law)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an answer that started before this section. It is not a new statement opening a new topic.

phrases.english: It is like the meal offering of the daily offerings.
phrases.notes: This finishes a thought from just before. Because the חביתין are like the תמידין, they also override שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier source for why the חביתין override שבת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חביתין share the status of the תמידין, which override שבת

steps.title: רבא: it needs a vessel, so baking a day early would disqualify it
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from 'on a griddle' that the חביתין need a holy vessel. If baked the day before, they would become פסול through לינה, so they must be baked on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'On a griddle' teaches that it needs a vessel. If he baked it the day before, it would become disqualified by being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new and different reason why the חביתין are baked even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the offering is made holy in a כלי שרת, it cannot be left overnight. Baking on Friday for שבת would make it פסול through לינה. So there is no option except baking on שבת, and that is why it overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat griddle or pan
It requires a (holy) vessel
Being left overnight, which makes holy things פסול
It becomes disqualified

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a pattern you will see often: when something cannot be done ahead of time, it may override שבת.

phrases.english: Rava said:
"On a griddle" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:14

phrases.english: teaches that it requires a vessel,
and if he bakes it from yesterday –
it becomes disqualified for him by being left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason for the same law as step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because it needs a holy vessel, baking a day early would disqualify it by לינה, so it must be baked on שבת

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also learns from 'on a griddle' that the חביתין need a vessel, just as רבא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught like רבא: 'On a griddle' teaches that it requires a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבא's first point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same words of the פסוק to teach that a vessel is needed. That is the starting point of רבא's whole argument. So רבא's reading has support from a תנאי source.

keyTerms.meaning: In agreement with him
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rava:
"On a griddle" –
teaches that it requires a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reading of the פסוק
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the חביתין require a vessel

steps.title: Extra oil is added, but how much?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: 'with the oil' teaches that extra oil is added, but the amount is not yet known.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With the oil' teaches that oil is added to it, but I do not know how much.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new detail of the פסוק, the oil. It raises a question about the amount, setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'the' oil shows that more oil than usual is added. The פסוק gives no number, though. So the ברייתא needs to find the amount from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: With the oil
To add
I do not know how much

phrases.english: "With the oil" –
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ויקרא 6:14. The word 'the' hints that there is extra oil.

phrases.english: to add oil to it,
but I do not know how much.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same ברייתא moves on to the oil
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much oil goes into the חביתין

steps.title: A גזרה שוה with the מנחת נסכים sets three לוגין
steps.stepSummary: The word 'oil' here is compared to 'oil' in the מנחת נסכים. Just as there it is three לוגין for each עשרון, so too here.
steps.simpleTranslation: I reason: 'oil' is said here, and 'oil' is said there about the libation meal offering. Just as there it is three log per tenth, so too here it is three log per tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question about the amount. It compares the same word in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both offerings use the word 'oil.' That links them in a גזרה שוה. The known amount from the מנחת נסכים, three לוגין per עשרון, would carry over to the חביתין. The next steps challenge this proposal.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reason it out
The meal offering brought with an animal קרבן and its wine
A liquid measure
A tenth of an איפה of flour
Learning one law from another through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: The חביתין override שבת. One reason is that they are like the תמידין. רבא's reason is that they need a vessel, so they cannot be baked early. For the oil, the ברייתא's first try is three לוגין per עשרון, learned from the מנחת נסכים. Steps 6-9 challenge this comparison until it ends in a tie, so it does not settle the amount by itself.

phrases.english: I reason:
"Oil" is stated here,
and "oil" is stated there regarding the libation meal offering –
phrases.notes: שמות 29:40, which says a quarter הין of oil for each עשרון. A הין is twelve לוגין, so that comes to three.

phrases.english: just as there it is three log per tenth,
so too here it is three log per tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how much oil
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three לוגין of oil per עשרון, learned by גזרה שוה from the מנחת נסכים

steps.title: A rival comparison: learn the oil from the voluntary meal offering
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the word שמן should be compared to the שמן of the מנחת נדבה, which uses only one לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: the Torah says 'oil' here, and it says 'oil' by the voluntary meal offering. Just as there it is one לוג, so too here it is one לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a second possible source for the amount of oil in the חביתין. This one gives a different answer: one לוג instead of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, שמן, also appears by the מנחת נדבה. So the word-link alone cannot decide between three לוגין and one לוג. This sets up the need to decide which offering is the better match.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way: an opening for a competing line of reasoning
A voluntary meal offering that a person chooses to bring
A liquid measure; here, the amount of oil per עשרון of flour

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. The ברייתא is raising a competing option so it can then weigh the two against each other.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, go this way:
It is stated here “oil,”
phrases.notes: "Here" means the חביתין of the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and it is stated by the voluntary meal offering “oil.”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1

phrases.english: Just as there it is one log,
so too here it is one log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5's comparison to the מנחת נסכים by offering an equally valid word-link to the מנחת נדבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison in step 5 to the מנחת נסכים (three לוגין).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word שמן also appears by the מנחת נדבה, which uses one לוג. So the word-link could point either way.

steps.title: The חביתין share four features with the מנחת נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא checks which offering is more similar. Like the מנחת נסכים, the חביתין are frequent, obligatory, override שבת, and override טומאה (תבש״ט).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which it is more like. We should learn something that has תבש״ט from something that has תבש״ט: frequent, brought as an obligation, overrides שבת, overrides טומאה. We should not learn something that has תבש״ט from something that does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts deciding between the two comparisons by asking which offering the חביתין resemble more. It lists four shared features with the מנחת נסכים, using a memory code.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters ת-ב-ש-ט stand for תדיר (offered every day), באה חובה (required), שבת (overrides שבת), טומאה (overrides טומאה). The חביתין and the מנחת נסכים share all four, and the מנחת נדבה has none of them. So the first argument favors three לוגין.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which it resembles: a test of which comparison fits better
Frequent; offered regularly, every day
Brought as a required obligation, not by choice
Overrides טומאה; may be brought even when the community is impure

phrases.english: Let us see to which it is similar?
We derive תבש״ט from תבש״ט:
phrases.notes: These four letters are a memory code. Each letter stands for one of the four features listed next.

phrases.english: frequent, brought as an obligation,
overrides Shabbat, overrides impurity.
And we do not derive תבש״ט from what is not תבש״ט.
phrases.notes: "What is not תבש״ט" is the מנחת נדבה, which has none of these four features.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing that the חביתין resemble the מנחת נסכים more, which supports step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חביתין share four features (תבש״ט) with the מנחת נסכים and none with the מנחת נדבה, so they should be learned from the מנחת נסכים.

steps.title: The חביתין also share four features with the מנחת נדבה
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe the חביתין are more like the מנחת נדבה: brought by an individual, for its own sake, without wine, with frankincense (יגי״ל).
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: we should learn something with יגי״ל from something with יגי״ל: an individual, brought for its own sake, wine, frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back with a list of four features the חביתין share with the מנחת נדבה. This puts the comparison back in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters י-ג-י-ל stand for יחיד (brought by one person), בגלל עצמה (brought on its own, not alongside an animal offering), יין (no wine libation with it), לבונה (it needs frankincense). The מנחת נסכים has the opposite of all four. So now each side has four points of similarity.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual; an offering of one person, not the whole community
Brought for its own sake, not as an add-on to another offering
Frankincense placed on certain meal offerings

steps.whyThisMatters: With four features on each side, simple similarity cannot settle the question. This sets up the need for a different way to decide.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, go this way:
We derive יגי״ל from יגי״ל:
an individual, for its own sake,
wine, frankincense.
phrases.notes: "Wine" means neither one comes with a wine libation. "Frankincense" means both of them need it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כְּלָךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: דָּנִין יגי״ל מיגי״ל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters step 7 with an equal list of features linking the חביתין to the מנחת נדבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that the חביתין clearly resemble the מנחת נסכים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חביתין share four different features (יגי״ל) with the מנחת נדבה, so the similarity argument does not clearly favor the מנחת נסכים.

steps.title: We cannot learn the יגי״ל offering from one that lacks יגי״ל
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the challenge from step 8. The חביתין share the יגי״ל traits with the מנחת נדבה, so we should not learn them from the מנחת נסכים, which lacks those traits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not learn an offering that has the יגי״ל traits from one that does not have the יגי״ל traits.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the counter-argument from step 8. Since the חביתין have the יגי״ל traits, it argues that we should not learn them from the מנחת נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 used the תבש״ט traits to link the חביתין to the מנחת נסכים (three לוגין). This line uses the יגי״ל traits to push back toward the מנחת נדבה (one לוג). Each side now has an equally strong comparison, so this whole method cannot settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: And we do not learn (one case from another)
Memory sign for traits shared with the מנחת נדבה: brought by an individual, for its own sake, without wine, with frankincense
From something that is not (like it)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא has now decided on one לוג. The point is that both comparisons are equally good, so this approach gets stuck. That is why new proofs come next.

phrases.english: And we do not learn an offering that has the יגי״ל traits
from one that does not have the יגי״ל traits.
phrases.notes: He means the מנחת נסכים, which lacks the traits listed in step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the counter-comparison begun in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the חביתין to the מנחת נסכים based on תבש״ט (step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The יגי״ל traits link the חביתין to the מנחת נדבה just as strongly, so we cannot learn them from the מנחת נסכים, which lacks those traits.

steps.title: The word תמיד links the חביתין to the daily offerings' מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה learns from the word תמיד that the חביתין follow the מנחת תמידין, which uses three לוגין for each עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: The פסוק says "fine flour for a meal offering perpetually (תמיד)." So the חביתין are like the meal offering of the daily offerings. Just as that meal offering uses three לוגין for each עשרון, so too this one uses three לוגין for each עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא offers a fresh proof that does not depend on comparing traits. He uses the word תמיד in the פסוק about the חביתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the חביתין 'תמיד', the same word used for the daily offerings. That shared word ties them together. So the חביתין take the oil amount of the מנחת תמידין: three לוגין for each עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour for a meal offering perpetually (from the פסוק about the חביתין)
The flour offering brought with the daily תמיד sacrifices
Plural of לוג, a measure of liquid
A tenth of an איפה, a measure of flour

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof gets around the deadlock between תבש״ט and יגי״ל. It uses a direct word link in the פסוק instead of weighing traits.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
"Fine flour for a meal offering perpetually":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13

phrases.english: so it is like the meal offering of the daily offerings.
Just as the meal offering of the daily offerings
has three log for each tenth,
so too this one has three log for each tenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the trait comparison ends in a tie, a new תנא proves the amount another way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חביתין use three לוגין of oil for each עשרון, learned from the word תמיד, which links them to the מנחת תמידין.

steps.title: Extra oil here and by the sheep's מנחה: three לוגין
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the תורה adds extra oil both by the חביתין and by the מנחת כבשים. Since the sheep's offering uses three לוגין for each עשרון, so do the חביתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The תורה added oil here, and it added oil by the meal offering of sheep. Just as there it is three לוגין for each עשרון, so too here it is three לוגין for each עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a third way to reach three לוגין. He compares the חביתין to the מנחה that comes with sheep offerings, because both get extra oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that both offerings get more oil than the normal amount. So the חביתין should match the sheep's מנחה, which uses three לוגין for each עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: Added more; the תורה gave extra (here, extra oil)
The flour offering brought with a sheep or lamb sacrifice

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The verse added oil here,
phrases.notes: Here means the חביתין, where 'with the oil' showed there is extra oil (step 4).

phrases.english: and it added oil in the meal offering of sheep.
Just as there it is three log for each tenth,
so too here it is three log for each tenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: רִיבָּה כָּאן שֶׁמֶן, וְרִיבָּה בְּמִנְחַת כְּבָשִׂים שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another תנא offers a different proof for the same three-לוג amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since both the חביתין and the מנחת כבשים get extra oil, the חביתין follow the sheep's amount: three לוגין for each עשרון.

steps.title: Maybe compare to the bulls' and rams' מנחה: only two לוגין
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון tests his own comparison. The מנחה of bulls and rams also gets extra oil, but it uses only two לוגין for each עשרון. So perhaps the חביתין should follow that amount instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps go this way: The תורה added oil here, and it added oil by the meal offering of bulls and rams. Just as there it is two לוגין for each עשרון, so too here it should be two לוגין for each עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון tests his own comparison. It points to another offering that also gets extra oil but uses a smaller amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's proof works only if the חביתין match the sheep's מנחה. But the bulls' and rams' מנחה also gets extra oil, and it uses only two לוגין for each עשרון. So the same reasoning could point to two לוגין instead of three.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way instead; a phrase that suggests a competing comparison
The flour offering brought with bull and ram sacrifices

phrases.english: Or perhaps, go this way:
The verse added oil here,
and it added oil in the meal offering of bulls and rams.
Just as there it is two log for each tenth,
so too here, two log for each tenth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון tests his own comparison from step 11 with a competing comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's comparison of the חביתין to the מנחת כבשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'extra oil' link also fits the מנחת פרים ואילים, which uses only two לוגין for each עשרון. So the same method could give a different amount.

steps.title: Compare by Amount of Flour: One Tenth to One Tenth
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the challenge from step 12. The חביתין use one עשרון of flour, so they should be learned from the sheep's מנחה, which also uses one עשרון. They should not be learned from the bulls' and rams' מנחה, which uses two or three עשרונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see which one it is more like. We learn a מנחה of one tenth from a מנחה of one tenth. We do not learn a מנחה of one tenth from a מנחה of two or three tenths.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון defends his own comparison. It says the sheep's מנחה is the better match for the חביתין, because both use the same amount of flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 there were two possible models, and both get extra oil. The tie-breaker is the amount of flour. The חביתין and the sheep's מנחה each use one עשרון, while the bulls' and rams' מנחה uses two or three. So the חביתין get three לוגין per עשרון, like the sheep's offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see which one it is more like; a formula for choosing between two possible comparisons
We derive or learn one case from another
One tenth of an איפה of flour, the standard amount for many מנחות
Tenths (plural), as in two or three tenths of an איפה

phrases.english: Let us see which it is more similar to:
We derive a meal offering that comes as one tenth
phrases.notes: This means the חביתין, which use one עשרון of flour.

phrases.english: from a meal offering that comes as one tenth,
phrases.notes: This is the מנחה that comes with the sheep.

phrases.english: and we do not derive a meal offering that comes as one tenth
from a meal offering that comes as two or three tenths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 12 by picking the closer comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the better comparison by a shared feature (the same amount of flour)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חביתין might follow the bulls' and rams' מנחה and get only two לוגין per עשרון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חביתין follow the sheep's מנחה, because both use one עשרון, so they get three לוגין per עשרון.

steps.title: The ברייתא Seems to Contradict Itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא first says 'בשמן' adds extra oil. Later it compares the חביתין to the מנחת נדבה, which uses only one לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. You said 'with the oil' comes to add oil to it. And then it teaches: 'oil' is said here, and 'oil' is said by the מנחת נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for contradicting itself between its opening and a later part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בשמן' teaches that the חביתין get more oil than usual, they cannot be learned from the מנחת נדבה, which has just one לוג. Yet the ברייתא later makes exactly that comparison, so its two parts seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
To add; here, to add extra oil beyond the normal amount
A voluntary meal offering, brought with one לוג of oil

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
you said "with the oil" is to add oil to it,
and then it teaches:
"Oil" is said here,
and "oil" is said by the voluntary meal offering.
phrases.notes: That comparison would give the חביתין only one לוג, like a מנחת נדבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the debate to point out a contradiction inside the ברייתא itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opening says 'בשמן' adds extra oil, but a later part compares the חביתין to the מנחת נדבה, which has the normal one לוג. Both cannot be right.

steps.title: אביי: Two Different תנאים in One ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the line 'בשמן adds oil' belongs to רבי שמעון, who is speaking in the style of 'if the פסוק had not said it.' The one who argues back with the comparison to the מנחת נדבה is רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Who taught that 'with the oil' comes to add? It is רבי שמעון, and he is speaking in the style of 'if it had not been said.' And who answers back with the logical argument? רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by assigning the different parts of the ברייתא to different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is saying that without the word 'בשמן,' we would have learned one לוג from the מנחת נדבה, so the word comes to add more. The comparison to the נדבה is only his 'what if' reasoning. רבי ישמעאל is the one who pushes back with that logical argument.

keyTerms.meaning: If it had not been said; a style of arguing about what we would think without a פסוק
A logical argument or comparison
Answers back, pushes back against

phrases.english: אביי said:
Who taught that "with the oil" is to add?
It is רבי שמעון,
and he is speaking in the style of "if it had not been said."
phrases.notes: He means: without the word בשמן we would have learned one לוג from the נדבה, so the word adds more.

phrases.english: And who answers back with the logical argument?
רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning different parts of the ברייתא to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא is one speaker who contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון says 'בשמן' adds oil, using 'if it had not been said' reasoning, and רבי ישמעאל is the one who argues back with the logical comparison.

steps.title: רב הונא: The Whole ברייתא Is One תנא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers differently. He says the entire ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: The whole thing is רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא offers a second answer to the contradiction: the whole ברייתא comes from one תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike אביי, רב הונא does not split the ברייתא between two speakers. He says all of it is רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, who in step 10 learned three לוגין per עשרון from the word תמיד.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it; the entire ברייתא
Continual; the word from which this תנא learns the חביתין's oil amount (step 10)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the ברייתא's contradiction. אביי says two תנאים are speaking: רבי שמעון ('בשמן' adds oil) and רבי ישמעאל (who argues back with the logical comparison). רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the whole ברייתא is רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said:
All of it is רבי ישמעאל

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא.
phrases.english: the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than אביי to the contradiction from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the entire ברייתא to a single תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must be split between רבי שמעון and רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: The word 'with the oil' comes to add extra oil
steps.stepSummary: Following רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, the ברייתא's first line means 'בשמן' adds more oil. A פסוק is not needed just to require oil, because 'על מחבת' already makes the חביתין like a מנחת מחבת, which has oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: 'With the oil' comes to add oil to it. If it only came to require oil at all, we would not need it. Since the פסוק says 'on a griddle,' it is already like a griddle offering, which has oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts walking through the ברייתא line by line to show how all of it fits רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. This first line explains why 'בשמן' must mean extra oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 14) it looked strange that the ברייתא says 'בשמן' adds oil and then compares the חביתין to the מנחת נדבה with only one לוג. Here we learn the first line is just the opening of his thinking: oil itself is already known from 'על מחבת', so 'בשמן' seems to teach more oil than usual.

keyTerms.meaning: to add more
to set or establish as a basic requirement
the meal offering made on a flat griddle, which has oil
it is like, it resembles

phrases.english: And this is what he is saying:
'With the oil' comes to add oil to it,
for if it were to establish that it has oil, it is not needed,
since it is written about it 'on a griddle',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:14

phrases.english: it is like a griddle meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's claim from step 16 works, starting with the first line of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא as one person's step-by-step reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first line and the later comparison seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first line is only the opening thought of רבי ישמעאל, which he will go on to test.

steps.title: Maybe 'with the oil' only teaches that oil is needed
steps.stepSummary: He then suggests another possibility: 'בשמן' might only teach that the חביתין need oil. Without it, we could have thought they are like a sinner's meal offering, which has no oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it only comes to establish that it has oil. If the Torah had not written 'with the oil,' I would have said it should be like a sinner's meal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside רבי ישמעאל's reasoning, he pushes back on his own first idea. He shows that 'בשמן' could have a simpler job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 17 depended on the idea that 'בשמן' had nothing else to teach. Now he finds another job for it: without 'בשמן' we might have treated the חביתין like the sinner's meal offering, which has no oil. That weakens the proof for extra oil.

keyTerms.meaning: the meal offering a poor sinner brings, which has no oil
I would have thought (an idea that turns out wrong)
'the Merciful One', meaning the Torah

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִקְבּוֹעַ לָהּ שֶׁמֶן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only to establish oil for it,
for if the Torah had not written 'with the oil',
I would have said: let it be like a sinner's meal offering.
phrases.notes: A sinner's meal offering has no oil at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִקְבּוֹעַ לָהּ שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on step 17 by giving 'בשמן' a different, simpler job.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof that 'בשמן' adds extra oil
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'בשמן' had no other job, but it may be needed to stop us from treating the חביתין like a sinner's offering.

steps.title: The comparison fails, so a פסוק is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל then says: even if 'בשמן' only requires oil, maybe we can get three לוגין by comparison. But that comparison does not work, so the פסוק 'סלת מנחה תמיד' is needed, as he says at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: let it even be only to establish oil. Let the amount come from a comparison. He tried the comparison, but it did not work for him. So the פסוק 'fine flour for a meal offering always' was needed, as רבי ישמעאל finishes his words.
steps.whatsHappening: He finishes his reasoning. He tries to learn the amount of oil by comparison, sees it fails, and ends with a פסוק that settles it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the whole ברייתא reads smoothly as one person thinking out loud. The line about the מנחת נדבה (one לוג) is the reason the comparison fails, since there is a comparison pulling toward one לוג too. So he needs 'סלת מנחה תמיד' to teach three לוגין, and the contradiction from step 14 is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: by reasoning or comparison, not from a direct פסוק
he needed a פסוק for it
'fine flour for a meal offering always', the פסוק about the חביתין
his statement, his words

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, the whole ברייתא is one person, רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, testing ideas one after another. In the end he needs the פסוק 'סלת מנחה תמיד' to learn that the חביתין get three לוגין.
steps.confusionAlert: The line comparing the חביתין to the מנחת נדבה is not his final opinion. It is the reason the comparison fails and why he needs a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר: תִּיהְוֵי נָמֵי לִקְבּוֹעַ לָהּ שֶׁמֶן,
phrases.english: He then said: let it even be to establish oil for it,
let it come from a comparison,
phrases.notes: He means: let the three לוגין be learned from the meal offering brought with the נסכים.

phrases.english: and he made the comparison, but it did not work for him,
phrases.notes: It fails because the comparison to the מנחת נדבה pulls the other way, toward one לוג.

phrases.english: and the verse 'fine flour for a meal offering always' was needed for it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:13

phrases.english: as רבי ישמעאל finishes his statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: תִּיהְוֵי נָמֵי לִקְבּוֹעַ לָהּ שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning after step 18 weakened the proof, and ends with the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the whole ברייתא is one consistent line of reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mix the view that 'בשמן' adds oil with a comparison to a one-לוג offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both lines are steps in רבי ישמעאל's reasoning, and the final source is 'סלת מנחה תמיד'.

steps.title: רבה: the whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a different answer. The whole ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who speaks in the style of 'if the פסוק had not said it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון, and he is speaking in the style of 'if it had not been said.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer to the problem from step 14. רבה says there is no change of speaker at all; it is all רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי split the ברייתא between two תנאים, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gave all of it to רבי ישמעאל. רבה gives all of it to רבי שמעון. The comparison to the מנחת נדבה is only what we would have thought if the פסוק had not been written, not a real argument against extra oil.

keyTerms.meaning: all of it, the whole ברייתא
'and if it had not been said', describing what we would think without the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to the problem in the ברייתא: אביי (split between רבי שמעון and רבי ישמעאל), רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע (all רבי ישמעאל), and רבה (all רבי שמעון, using 'if it had not been said').

phrases.english: רבה said: All of it is רבי שמעון
[and he is speaking in the style of 'if it had not been said'].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are part of the corrected wording; some versions leave them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the problem from step 14, unlike those of אביי (step 15) and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע (steps 16-19).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the whole ברייתא to one speaker, read as 'if it had not been said'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to the מנחת נדבה looked like someone arguing against רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is רבי שמעון himself describing what we would have thought without the פסוק.

steps.title: Why 'with the oil' must mean extra oil
steps.stepSummary: Following רבה, רבי שמעון reads 'בשמן' as adding extra oil to the חביתין. A פסוק is not needed just to require oil, since 'על מחבת' makes them like a מנחת מחבת. He also claims that even without 'בשמן', he could derive the extra oil by a דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי שמעון means: 'with the oil' comes to add more oil. If it only meant that oil is required, we would not need it, because the פסוק says 'on a griddle,' so the offering is like a griddle meal offering, which has oil. And even before 'with the oil' is said, I could figure out the extra oil by reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins explaining the first line of the ברייתא according to רבי שמעון. The word 'בשמן' teaches extra oil, not just that oil is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Basic oil is already known from 'על מחבת', because the חביתין are compared to a מנחת מחבת. So 'בשמן' must teach something new: more oil than usual. רבי שמעון then adds in his typical style that he could have reached even this through a דין, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To add, meaning extra oil beyond the normal amount
To establish, meaning to set the basic requirement that oil is needed
A griddle or pan; also the name of a meal offering made on one, which has oil
It is similar to; it is compared to
I have it by reasoning; I can derive it without the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This explanation sounds a lot like רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's version in step 17. The difference is who is speaking. Here the whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון, using his style of 'even if the פסוק had not said it, I could derive it.'

phrases.english: And this is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי שמעון, as רבה explained in step 20.

phrases.english: 'With the oil' is to add more oil to it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי לִקְבּוֹעַ לָהּ שֶׁמֶן לָא צְרִיךְ,
phrases.english: for if it were just to establish oil for it, that would not be needed,
since it is written about it 'on a griddle,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:14

phrases.english: it is like a griddle meal offering,
phrases.notes: A griddle meal offering already has oil, so the basic oil is covered.

phrases.english: and even before 'with the oil' is said,
I have it by reasoning.
phrases.notes: He means he could reach the extra oil through a דין, even without the word 'בשמן'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רבה's approach from step 20, applied to the first line of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא according to one תנא (רבי שמעון) and his style of speaking
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בשמן' might only teach that the חביתין need oil
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בשמן' teaches extra oil, since basic oil is already known from 'על מחבת'

steps.title: The derivation fails, so the bulls-and-rams comparison is tried
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's derivation for extra oil does not work, so 'בשמן' is needed to teach extra oil. He then suggests the amount: the חביתין should be like the מנחה brought with bulls and rams.
steps.simpleTranslation: He tried the reasoning, but it did not work for him, so the word 'with the oil' was needed. Then he said: let it be like the meal offering of bulls and rams.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון admits his reasoning fails, so the פסוק's word 'בשמן' really is needed. He then tries to figure out how much extra oil by comparing to the bulls-and-rams offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'בשמן' has a clear job: it teaches that the חביתין need more oil than usual. It still does not say how much more. So רבי שמעון suggests copying the amount used in the מנחה that comes with bulls and rams, which also has extra oil.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a derivation; he tried to reason it out
It did not work for him; the reasoning failed
He needed it; the פסוק became necessary
The meal offering brought with bull and ram sacrifices, which has extra oil

phrases.english: And he made the derivation, but it did not work for him,
so he needed 'with the oil,'

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר: תֶּיהְוֵי כְּמִנְחַת פָּרִים וְאֵילִים.
phrases.english: He then said: Let it be like the meal offering of bulls and rams.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the derivation claimed in step 21 fails, which explains why 'בשמן' is needed, and then moves on to the amount
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the flow of the ברייתא as a chain of attempted derivations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Extra oil could be derived by reasoning alone
steps.terutzMaskana: The reasoning fails, so 'בשמן' teaches the extra oil, and a comparison is needed for the amount

steps.title: Starting a new derivation
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון begins a new line of reasoning ('we derive...'), apparently moving away from the bulls-and-rams comparison. The גמרא finishes this sentence on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: We derive...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי שמעון starts a new derivation, and the גמרא completes it on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הדר אמר' show another turn in his thinking. It appears he will learn the oil amount from a different source than bulls and rams. The full reasoning comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive; we learn one case from another

phrases.english: He then said: We derive

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attempt that follows the bulls-and-rams suggestion in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Continuing the chain of derivations in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The amount comes from the bulls-and-rams offering
steps.terutzMaskana: A different derivation is about to be offered (finished in the next lines)
